_about: Destruction-economy tunables.
EVERY NUMBER HERE IS A GUESS. The original's constants live inside AngelScript
bytecode we can name but not yet read - see docs/original-gameplay.md section 5.
WHAT IS ESTABLISHED (structure, from level data + binary identifiers):
- Four flags drive everything, read through one predicate the binary names
isBreakableOrExplosiveOrBurnable: demolisher / explosive / burnable / breakable.
- demolisher appears ONLY on rolling_stone (27/27 placements).
- explosive appears ONLY on barrel_bomb (31/31).
- burning REMOVES the body entirely, collision included - that removal is the
puzzle, since burning a crate deletes a platform or a blocker. Five chapter-2
achievements are gated on burning, or not burning, a specific crate.
- Burning is reversible upstream (healBurn, extinguish_fire.ent,
playFireExtinguishSound). NOT modelled: nothing in the level data puts a fire out.
- A shock_agent's ring is DRAWN at radius areaRadius (shock_area.ent, white_ring.png
at 128px, so scale = areaRadius/64). It is an honest read-out of the danger zone,
so it must be visible or the hazard is unfair.
- A carranca fires the entity in its `entity` key (always fireball.ent) along
(dirX,dirY): first shot after startStride ms, then every stride ms. Both are bare
uints with no `speed`, hence milliseconds - and startStride existing alongside
stride is what proves the millisecond reading for this whole family.

burning._note: Long enough to be a race the player can win or lose; not measured.

explosion._note: Chains to other explosives. Radius invented; explosion_small/huge both exist.

_note: fire_agent has NO physics body (shape=BS_NONE) - only a 38x38 legacy AABB, so 24px
is roughly half that box. Ticked on a staggered timer, never per frame (rule 6).
Chapter 4 only - the zero-gravity chapter, where a well is the only thing that
moves loose objects. Linear falloff rather than inverse-square: stable at the
centre and more predictable in a puzzle. Both the law and the number are guesses.

turret._note: Carranca fireballs. Speed and lifetime invented; direction comes from data.
